images.title: The gap in the circle
images.purpose: Set up the question: a circle holds a 1/2 piece and a 1/3 piece, and the student finds the fractional unit that fills the gap by subtracting from 1 in a common unit.
images.composition: One large circle in the centre left with wide space around it, and one question line on the right.
images.exact_structure: One large flat circle, the whole, with a dark outline. One teal #0072B2 sector fills exactly one half of the circle (180 degrees). Next to it, one amber #E69F00 sector fills exactly one third of the circle (120 degrees). The remaining sector is empty, outlined with a reddish purple #CC79A7 dashed line, with a large question mark inside it. Thin grey #6B7280 lines mark the sector edges from the centre. Right: one question line. Exactly 1 circle, 1 teal sector, 1 amber sector, 1 empty sector.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any fraction written in or beside the empty sector, or sectors not in the stated sizes
images.takeaway: Find the gap by subtracting in one common unit.
images.description: A circle holding a teal half and an amber third, with the last sector empty and marked with a question mark; the question asks what fills the gap. No answer is shown.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to name a unit that both 1/2 and 1/3 can be written in before finding the gap.

image_decisions.why: A circle with two pieces and a marked gap shows the question at a glance without naming the missing unit.
